summary: Joanny Grosset was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon, where he earned a Licencié-ès-lettres and studied under Paul Regnaud.

Joaquim Heliodoro da Cunha Rivara was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied mathematics, philosophy, and medicine at the University of Coimbra (1824–1836) and served as a teacher and librarian at Liceu de Évora (~1838–1855).

Jochem Schindler was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Heinz Kronasser and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Würzburg, later holding positions at Vienna and Harvard University.

Joe Bransford Wilson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Virginia in 1984, where he also taught (1981–1985), and served as Associate Professor at the University of North Carolina Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of London, he served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010) and President of the Royal Numismatic Society (2005–2009).
Joe Currie is an Indology and religious studies scholar who held a post at Harvard University, where he is attested as a Ph.D. candidate in 2026.

Joel Bordeaux is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed his MA, MPhil, and PhD at Columbia University. He has held teaching posts at Colgate, Stony Brook, Leiden, and Utrecht universities, as well as Erasmus University Rotterdam.

Joel Peter Brereton is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Stanley Insler in 1971. He held academic posts at the University of Missouri (1999–2000) and the University of Texas at Austin (~2001, 2004).
Joel Tatelman is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Oxford in 1996 under Alexis Sanderson.
Joen Imai is a Buddhist studies scholar who held the post of professor at Shuchiin University, attested in 2010 and 2026.

Joerg Tuske is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held a post at the University of Cambridge (attested 1998) and served as an Associate Professor of Philosophy at Salisbury University (attested 2013).

Joey Hung is a scholar in computational and Buddhist studies who attended the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts. He has held posts at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar was a historian and Indologist who studied at Bangabasi College and Presidency University. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, and Patna College, and became a University Reader at Patna University in 1923.
Johan Andreas dèr Mouw was a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University (1883–1887).

Johan Elverskog specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at UC Berkeley and Indiana University Bloomington, he became Dedman Family Distinguished Professor and Professor of Religious Studies at Southern Methodist University (~2000).

Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht, Leiden, and Berlin under Antonie Rutgers and Albrecht Weber. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University before serving as Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1865–1903).

Johan Hendrik Gallée was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University (1866–1873). He taught at Stedelijk Gymnasium Haarlem and served as a lektor at Utrecht University (1881–1892).

Johan Hendrik Kern was a linguist who studied at Leiden, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He served as Professor of English, Russian, and Sanskrit at the University of Groningen (1901–1924) and later as Professor of Dutch at Leiden University (1924–1933).

Johan Huizinga worked in history, Indology, and linguistics, earning a Ph.D. at Groningen and studying at Leipzig and Leiden. He taught at the University of Amsterdam, Groningen (1905–1915), and Leiden University (1915–1941) as Professor of History.
